## Limits

Tool results use up the model’s context window, so each kind of result
has a cap. `MAX_TOOL_CHARS` caps one result, and is sized for the
smallest model in use. Tool factories take the cap as `mx`, so a harness
running a larger model can raise it. `MAX_HITS` caps search hits,
`MAX_GREP_HITS` exact `grep` matches, `MAX_API` the names a `public_api`
listing returns, and `MAX_FILE` the size of a file worth reading as
source at all.

``` python
# a grep answers with more rows than a search, because an exact match is cheaper to read
assert MAX_GREP_HITS > MAX_HITS
assert MAX_TOOL_CHARS < 8_000 and MAX_FILE > MAX_TOOL_CHARS
test_eq((MAX_TOOL_CHARS, MAX_HITS, MAX_GREP_HITS, MAX_API, MAX_FILE), (6000, 20, 60, 200, 2_000_000))
```

Every search backend returns its results as
[`Hit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#hit)s: the path,
line, symbol and matching text.

## Failure

A tool must not raise, because an exception ends the agent’s turn. A
tool that fails returns a string starting with `ERROR:` instead, so the
model can read what went wrong and try again.
[`err`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#err) builds that
string,
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#failed) checks
for it, and
[`host_err`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#host_err)
formats an exception as `Type: message`.
[`HostError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#hosterror)
is the exception a host raises to refuse something.

`attempt(what, f)` is the `try`/`except` every tool would otherwise
repeat. It runs `f` and turns any exception into an
[`err`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#err), except
`NotImplementedError`, which it lets through: that means the host cannot
do this at all, which the caller handles differently from a call that
failed. [`Media`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#media)
is a result string that also carries pictures, as paths or bytes, which
the agent’s loop sends to the model after the text.

```

## The read guard

An application may need to control what reaches the model, for example
to keep personal data away from a hosted model while letting a local one
see it. A host’s `read_guard`, when set, is a function every read tool
calls before sending content. It receives a
[`ReadCheck`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#readcheck)
describing the read: the `path` (a URL or page id for web reads), the
`tool`, the `kind` of content (`text`, `hits`, `cell`, `diff`, `url`,
`page` or `image`), the turn’s `model`, whether that model runs
`local`ly, and `text`, the content the tool would send. `text` is loaded
only if the guard asks for it, so a guard that decides by path reads
nothing. `local` is None when the host cannot tell, and a guard should
then treat the model as hosted.

The guard returns None or True to send the content unchanged, a string
to send instead (a masked version, or even an empty string), or a
[`Refusal`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#refusal);
False is a refusal with the default wording. A guard that raises refuses
the read with kind `guard_failed`. A refusal reaches the model as an
`ERROR:` result naming its kind, path and reason, so
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#failed)
recognises it. `model` and `local` come from the host’s `model_local()`,
which returns `(local, model)`.

Tools call the guard through two helpers.
[`guard_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#guard_read)
returns None (send as is), a replacement string, or a
[`Refusal`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#refusal).
[`screened`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#screened)
returns the text to send, or the
[`Refusal`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#refusal).
With no guard set,
[`guard_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#guard_read)
returns None without calling anything and
[`screened`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#screened)
returns the text unchanged.

### ReadCheck

def ReadCheck(
    path, tool:str='', kind:str='text', load:NoneType=None, model:str='', local:NoneType=None

```

*One read for a `read_guard` to decide on; `text` is loaded only when

``` python
class _H: read_guard = model_local = None
h = _H()
test_eq(guard_read(h, '/a.md', lambda: 1/0), None)              # no guard: nothing is called
test_eq(screened(h, '/a.md', 'secret'), 'secret')
seen = []
def guard(r):
    seen.append(r)
    if r.path.endswith('open.md'): return None
    if r.path.endswith('local.md'): return Refusal('local-only, and this model is hosted') if not r.local else True
    if r.path.endswith('boom.md'): raise RuntimeError('vault closed')
    if r.path.endswith('no.md'): return False
    return r.text.replace('ada@x.org', '[EMAIL]')
h.read_guard, h.model_local = guard, lambda: (False, 'claude-opus')
loads = []
test_eq(screened(h, '/open.md', 'ada@x.org'), 'ada@x.org')
test_eq(guard_read(h, '/open.md', lambda: loads.append(1)), None); test_eq(loads, [])   # decided on the path, read nothing
test_eq(screened(h, '/p.md', 'mail ada@x.org'), 'mail [EMAIL]')
test_eq((seen[-1].model, seen[-1].local, seen[-1].kind), ('claude-opus', False, 'text'))
r = screened(h, '/local.md', 'x')
test_eq((type(r), r.kind, r.path, str(r)), (Refusal, 'withheld', '/local.md', 'ERROR: withheld: /local.md: local-only, and this model is hosted'))
test_eq(failed(str(r)), True)
test_eq(screened(h, '/local.md', 'x', local=True), 'x')          # a per-call model overrides the turn's
test_eq(str(screened(h, '/no.md', 'x')), 'ERROR: withheld: /no.md: this host withholds it from this model')
test_eq(screened(h, '/boom.md', 'x').kind, 'guard_failed')
h.model_local = lambda: 1/0
screened(h, '/p.md', 'x'); test_eq((seen[-1].model, seen[-1].local), ('', None))   # unknown model: local is None
```

## The sandbox

The sandbox keeps tools inside the folders the user opened, called
roots. Each path is resolved before it is checked, so `..`, `~` and
symbolic links are judged by where they actually lead.
[`Sandbox`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#sandbox) does
this and raises
[`Unsafe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#unsafe), a
[`HostError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#hosterror),
for a path it refuses. Each host keeps one
[`Sandbox`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#sandbox) and
every tool goes through it.

Some paths are refused even when reads outside the roots are allowed.
`DENY` lists them: SSH and cloud credentials, `.env` files, private keys
and similar.
[`denied`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#denied) checks
a path against that list, ignoring case, because a case-insensitive disk
opens `.SSH` as `.ssh`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/core.py#L108"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### spill_dir

``` python
def spill_dir():
```

*The private folder, one per process, where results too long to send
whole are saved; every
[`Sandbox`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#sandbox) may
read it and none may write it.*

`Sandbox(roots)` opens folders for reading and writing, and `read_roots`
folders for reading only. `check(path)` resolves a path, relative to the
first root if it is relative, and returns it or raises
[`Unsafe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#unsafe). A
path that does not exist yet still resolves, since a tool creating a
file needs that; readers pass `must_exist=True`. `reading=True` marks a
read, which may use read-only roots and `read_outside`. `covers` and
`reads` test a path against the two kinds of root, `add_root` and
`drop_root` open and close folders, `root_of` names the root holding a
path, and `bare` and `under` handle a file name given by a person or a
model.

A result too long to send whole can be saved with
[`spill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#spill), which
writes it to the folder
[`spill_dir`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#spill_dir)
names and returns the path. Every sandbox may read that folder, so the
model can page through the full result with `view_file`, and none may
write to it.

``` python
tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
root = Path(tmp.name).resolve()/'proj'
(root/'pkg').mkdir(parents=True)
(root/'pkg'/'a.py').write_text('x = 1\n')

sb = Sandbox([root])
sb.check('pkg/a.py').name, sb.check('pkg/new.py').name, sb.covers(root/'pkg'), sb.root_of('pkg/a.py') == root
```

Resolving before checking is what stops a symbolic link from escaping:
checking the unresolved path would accept `link/secret.txt` because it
looks inside the root. With no open folders nothing resolves, so a host
cannot be tricked into reading `/etc/passwd`.

``` python
outside = Path(tmp.name).resolve()/'outside'
outside.mkdir()
(outside/'secret.txt').write_text('token\n')
(root/'link').symlink_to(outside, target_is_directory=True)

test_fail(lambda: sb.check('link/secret.txt'), contains=SANDBOX)        # a symlink out
test_fail(lambda: sb.check('../outside/secret.txt'), contains=SANDBOX)  # .. traversal
test_fail(lambda: sb.check(outside/'secret.txt'), contains=SANDBOX)     # an absolute path elsewhere
test_fail(lambda: sb.check('pkg/new.py', must_exist=True), contains='no such file')
test_fail(lambda: Sandbox().check('/etc/passwd'), contains=NO_ROOTS)    # nothing open, nothing readable
```

`read_outside=True` widens reads only. Writes must still land in an open
folder, and credential paths are always refused.

``` python
lax = Sandbox([root], read_outside=True)
lax.check(outside/'secret.txt', reading=True).name
```

Open folders never nest. Opening a parent closes the roots inside it,
and opening a folder already covered changes nothing, so each file is
walked and indexed once.

``` python
sb2 = Sandbox([root/'pkg', root])                         # a folder and its parent, opened together
[r.name for r in sb2.roots]
```

`bare` refuses a name that is really a path, such as `../../etc`.
`under` places a named entry inside a folder without letting it escape.

``` python
sb.under('pkg', 'b.py').name, sb.bare('b.py')
```

## Clipping

Long results have to be cut to fit the budget, and the cut should tell
the model what it missed.
[`clip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#clip) shortens a
string to `n` characters, at a line break when one is close, and appends
a note giving how much was shown. The note counts against `n`. `more`
adds a hint on how to read the rest, and `keep=True` saves the whole
result with
[`spill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#spill) and
names the file in the note.
[`clip_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#clip_json)
does the same for JSON while keeping it valid JSON: a list keeps the
items that fit plus a last item saying how many more there are, and a
dict keeps its plain fields, with the longest strings shortened and a
`truncated` note.

``` python
import re
```

``` python
test_eq(clip('short', 12), 'short')
five = 'one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\n' * 3
test_eq(clip(five, 60).splitlines()[0], 'one')
assert len(clip(five, 60)) <= 60, 'the note counts against the budget'
kept = clip(five, 60, keep=True)
saved = Path(re.search(r'saved to (\S+?);', kept).group(1))
test_eq(saved.read_text(), five)
assert len(kept) <= 200 and 'view_file' in kept
report = {'undo': 'u1', 'head': 'abc123', 'branches': [f'branch-{i}' for i in range(200)]}
small = json.loads(clip_json(report, 500))                     # still a document a harness can parse
test_eq((small['undo'], small['head'], 'branches' in small), ('u1', 'abc123', False))
test_eq(json.loads(Path(re.search(r'saved to (\S+?);', small['truncated']).group(1)).read_text()), report)
test_eq(json.loads(clip_json({'undo': 'u1'})), {'undo': 'u1'})
long_result = clip_json({'undo': 'u1', 'result': 'r' * 5000, 'branches': ['b']}, 600)   # a long plain field is shortened, not kept whole
assert len(long_result) <= 600 and json.loads(long_result)['undo'] == 'u1', long_result
commits = [{'sha': f'{i:07d}', 'subject': 'x' * 40} for i in range(100)]
log = clip_json(commits, 800)                                    # a list stays a list: what fits, then a note
assert len(log) <= 800 and isinstance(json.loads(log), list) and 'more' in json.loads(log)[-1], log[-200:]
test_eq(clip('hello', 5), 'hello')
assert clip('hello', 0).startswith('h') and '1 of 5' in clip('hello', 0)   # a zero or negative budget
assert clip('hello', -200).startswith('h')
```

[`clip_lines`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#clip_lines)
renders a list of lines within `n` characters and says which line to
continue from, which is how `view_file` pages through a file. `more` is
the hint, and `{next}` in it is replaced by the next line number.
`empty` is returned for an empty list. A single line longer than the
budget is cut by characters, and the note gives its length but no line
to resume from.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/core.py#L227"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### clip_lines

``` python
def clip_lines(
    lines, start:int=1, n:int=6000, more:str='', empty:str='(nothing)'
):
```

*Render `lines` within `n` chars, the note included whenever `n` is
longer than the note, and say which line to resume from.*

``` python
print(clip_lines([f'def f{i}(): pass' for i in range(20)], n=200, more='read from line {next}'))
```

``` python
test_eq(clip_lines([], empty='(no matches)'), '(no matches)')
test_eq(clip_lines(['a', 'b'], n=100), 'a\nb')
long = clip_lines(['x' * 500], n=200)
assert long.startswith('x' * 100) and '500 chars' in long and len(long) <= 200, long
paged = clip_lines([f'line {i}' for i in range(100)], n=200, more='read from line {next}')
assert len(paged) <= 200 and 'read from line' in paged, paged
hinted = clip_lines(['x' * 50] * 40, n=1000, more='m' * 600)        # a long hint is reserved whole, not capped at half the budget
assert len(hinted) <= 1000 and hinted.endswith('m]'), len(hinted)
```

## Edits

A model sends edits as lists, because the tool schemas declare them as
arrays, and a harness may pass a stray JSON string through.
[`cmds`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#cmds) parses
commands for exhash, the hash-addressed editor, into the tuples it
expects. [`edits`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#edits)
parses exact-text replacements. Both reject input they cannot read with
an error that names the shape wanted.

<a

### cmds

``` python
def cmds(
    commands
):
```

*Parse exhash `commands`, as JSON or lists, into the tuples exhash
expects, nested lists included.*

``` python
cmds('[["12|a1b2|", "s", "old", "new"], ["30|9f3c|", "a", "appended"]]')
```

``` python
test_eq(cmds([['1|ab|', 'd']]), [('1|ab|', 'd')])
test_fail(lambda: cmds('{"not": "a list"}'), contains='must be a JSON list')
test_fail(lambda: cmds('["bare string"]'), contains='must be an array')
```

[`edits`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#edits) accepts
a list of `{oldText, newText}` dicts, a list of `[old, new]` pairs, or a
single dict. A JSON string of any of those is still accepted in this
release.
[`apply_edits`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#apply_edits)
applies them to a text. Each `oldText` must appear exactly once, and the
edits must not overlap. Otherwise it raises a `ValueError` naming the
edit and how to fix it: give the exact text, add surrounding lines when
a match is ambiguous, or merge overlapping edits.

### edits

``` python
def edits(
    es
):
```

*`{'oldText','newText'}` dicts or `[old, new]` pairs, as a list; a JSON
string of either still parses this release.*

``` python
before = 'def greet(name):\n    return "hello " + name\n'
after = apply_edits(before, edits([{'oldText': 'hello', 'newText': 'howdy'}]))
after
```

``` python
test_eq(edits([{'oldText': 'a', 'newText': 'b'}]), [('a', 'b')])
test_eq(edits([['a', 'b']]), [('a', 'b')]); test_eq(edits({'oldText': 'a', 'newText': 'b'}), [('a', 'b')])
test_eq(edits('[{"oldText": "a", "newText": "b"}]'), [('a', 'b')])            # a string still parses this release
test_fail(lambda: edits('not json'), contains='list of {"oldText"')
test_fail(lambda: edits([{'old_text': 'a', 'new_text': 'b'}]), contains="'oldText' and 'newText'")
test_fail(lambda: edits([['a']]), contains='[old, new]')
test_fail(lambda: edits(3), contains='list of')
try: apply_edits(before, [('', 'x')])
except ValueError as e: assert 'oldText is empty' in str(e) and 'create_file' not in str(e), e   # the message is one both editors can carry
test_eq(after, 'def greet(name):\n    return "howdy " + name\n')
```

Here are the three refusals on real text. Each message tells the model
how to correct the edit, not only that it failed.

``` python
refusals = [lambda: apply_edits(before, [('name', 'who')]), lambda: apply_edits(before, [('nowhere', 'x')]), lambda: apply_edits(before, [('def greet', 'def hi'), ('greet(name)', 'hi(n)')])]
for r in refusals:
    try: r()
    except Exception as ex: print(host_err(ex))
```

[`diff_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#diff_text)
makes the unified diff that edit tools return and that approval prompts
show a person.

### diff_text

``` python
def diff_text(
    before, after, path:str='file'
):
```

*A unified diff from `before` to `after`, labelled with `path`.*

``` python
print(diff_text(before, after, 'greet.py'))
```

``` python
assert '-    return "hello " + name' in diff_text(before, after)
assert diff_text(before, before) == ''
```

## Which tools write

An application usually asks a person before a tool changes something.
`@writes` marks a tool as one that does, and
[`is_write`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#is_write)
checks the mark. `WRITE_TOOLS` lists the same tools by name, for a
caller that only has a name; the tests check that the two agree. `@acts`
and
[`has_effect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#has_effect)
mark tools that act without writing a file the user owns, such as
running an API call or starting a watch, and `ACTING_TOOLS` names them.
Approval does not gate these, but a sub-agent told not to act loses them
too. The git tools are listed in `GIT_READ_TOOLS` and `GIT_WRITE_TOOLS`.

`@summary` attaches a function that turns a call’s arguments into the
one line a person reads after the tool runs, such as “Edit pkg/a.py”.
[`summarise`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#summarise)
produces that line for a tool or a bare tool name, falling back to
`name(arg=value, ...)`. It finds summaries for bare names in
`SUMMARIES`, which `shalya.tools` fills when it is imported.
[`one_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#one_line)
squeezes any value onto one short line.

### writes

``` python
def writes(
    f
):
```

*Mark tool `f` as one that changes something, so an approval step can
put it in front of a person.*

``` python
@writes
def create_file(path, text): return f'wrote {path}'
def view_file(path): return 'contents'
is_write(create_file), is_write(view_file)
```

``` python
test_eq(is_write(create_file), True)
test_eq(is_write(view_file), False)
test_eq(create_file.__name__ in WRITE_TOOLS, True)
test_eq(sorted(GIT_TOOLS), sorted(set(GIT_READ_TOOLS) | GIT_WRITE_TOOLS))
test_eq(GIT_READ_TOOLS, ('git_status', 'git_divergence', 'git_diff', 'git_log'))
assert {'watch', 'research', 'inspect_python'} <= ACTING_TOOLS and not ({'watch_url', 'set_reminder'} & ACTING_TOOLS)
assert 'edit_file' in WRITE_TOOLS and 'watch' not in WRITE_TOOLS
```
